4. Writ-respondent No. 4 contested the Rule Nisi by filing affidavit-in-opposition con-tending, inter alia, that writ-respondent No. 4 was Senior to the writ-petitioner inasmuch as writ-respondent No. 4 joined BARI on 15-8-2006 in the post of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) directly which is a permanent post in the Revenue Budget of BARI and the authority, by its order dated 8-3-2007, regularised the service of writ-respondent No. 4 with effect from 15-8-2006. On the other hand, the writ-petitioner joined a Development Project under the name and style "Horticulture Development Project" in 1997 and subsequently the writ-petitioner's post was temporarily transferred to the Revenue Budget and he was temporarily appointed in the Revenue set-up; albeit his post was not included in বাংলাদেশ কৃষি গবেষণা ইনষ্টিটিউট (কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯০ (briefly the service Regulations of 1990) and in the BARI organogram. However, the post of the writ-petitioner was created and included in বাংলাদেশ কৃষি গবেষণা ইনষ্টিটিউট (কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ২০১১ (hereinafter referred to as the Service Regulations of 2011) and his post was made permanent by the order of the Ministry of Agriculture under Memo No. গবেষণা-১/চাকুরী/রাজস্বখাত-২৮/২০০০ dated 23-1-2012 with effect from 1-6-2012. The writ-petitioner was appointed as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in the Development Project, namely, “উদ্যান উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প (বারী অংশ)” and the duration of the project expired on 31-12-1999. Thereafter the Ministry of Agriculture, by its Memo No. কৃম-৩/চাকুরী (রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তর)-২৮/২০০৩/৭২০ dated 4-11-2003, temporarily transferred 44 (forty-four) posts including the post of the writ-petitioner to the Revenue Budget and gave sanction on year-to-year retention basis with retrospective effect from 1-1-2000 under certain terms and conditions. Subsequently the BARI authority, without following the terms and conditions mentioned in the Memo dated 4-11-2003 issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and violating the relevant provisions, directly appointed the writ-petitioner to the post of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) on temporary retention basis by its Memo No. ২প-৫/২০০৫/প্রশাসন/৯৮১২ dated 16-4-2005. At that point of time, there were 2 (two) posts of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in the BARI organogram and, as such„ the BARI authority in his appointment letter imposed a condition to the effect that “রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তরিত সহকারী পরিচালক (অর্থ ও হিসাব) পদটি স্থায়ী হওয়ার পর সন্তোষজনকভাবে কার্য সম্পাদন সাপেক্ষে তাহাকে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী করা হইবে।” Since the writ-petitioner's post was created and included in the Service Regulations of 2011, there was no scope to regularise his service prior thereto. Besides, before regularisation of the service of the writ-petitioner, the BARI authority did not take any approval from the Selection Committee or the DPC, as the case may be, which was mandatory for regularisation of his service as per “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” (hereinafter referred to as the Rules of 2005). So the order of regularisation dated 24-5-2006 of the service of the writ-petitioner is illegal. Writ-respondent No. 4 raised an objection to the alleged seniority of the writ-petitioner and made an application to the Director-General of BARI for fixation of inter se seniority. On the basis of that application submitted by writ-respondent No. 4, the Director-General of BARI formed a high-powered three-member committee by his order under Memo No. বি-৬৪৬/২০১২/প্রশাসন/১২৯৪ dated 6-8-2012. That committee asked the writ-petitioner and writ-respondent No. 4 to submit their respective papers and documents and accordingly they submitted the same. The committee perused the papers and documents and found that some irregularities had been committed at the time of regularisation of service and fixation of seniority of the writ-petitioner and accordingly the committee made a report dated 5-9-2012 and submitted the same to the Director-General of BARI under Memo No. 452 dated 6-9-2012 recommending fixation of the two contestants' inter se seniority by the Ministry of Public Administration. But nonetheless, the BARI authority promoted the writ-petitioner to the post of Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) by the order dated 9-9-2012. 

 11. Mr AM Aminuddin, learned Senior Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that on harmonious reading of Chapter-7 of the Probidhanmala, it is very much clear that the appeal as provided in Rule 46 relates to an order passed for violating any office discipline awarding punishment and not for any other matter such as promotion, and hence the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that the appeal of writ-respondent No. 4 to the Government was not maintainable. He further submitted that on harmonious reading of regulations 46 and 47 of the Probidhanmala, it is abundantly clear that the appeal provided in regulation 46 is only relating to the order awarding punishment and the review provided in Regulation 47 is against any order, consequently the order passed by the Government on the basis of an appeal filed by writ-respondent No. 4 was devoid of any jurisdiction. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering that the Service of the writ-petitioner after transfer to the revenue budget was regularised along with 6 others on 24-5-2006 and the said decision was considered in the 50th and 51st General Meeting of the Board of Management which is the highest decision making authority of BARI. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not considering that the writ-petitioner joined in the development project in the year 1997 and he was later transferred to the revenue budget on 04-11-2003 with effect from 1-1-2000, and he was posted in his post on 24-5-2006 and thereafter was regularised in the post on 24-5-2006 and writ-respondent No. 4 having joined in his post after the regularisation of the writ-petitioner, the writ-petitioner is senior to writ-respondent No. 4. He further submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in discharging the Rule without considering the fact that the service of the writ-petitioner is governed by a specific service rule namely   “বাংলাদেশ কৃষি গবেষণা ইনষ্টিটিউট (কর্মকর্তা-কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ২০১১” and the writ-petitioner being an employee of Bangladesh Agricultural Research Institute and not in the service of the Republic, the provision “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেটে স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জ্যেষ্ঠতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫” has no manner of application in the service of the employees working under statutory body like the writ-petitioner. 

 13. Mr Zainul Abedin, learned Advocate-on- Record appearing for writ-respondent No. 4 submitted that writ-respondent No. 4 is senior to the writ-petitioner, inasmuch as writ-respondent No. 4 joined BARI on 15-8-2006 in the post of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) directly, which is a permanent post in the Revenue Budget of BARI and the authority by its order dated 8-3-2007 regularised the service of writ-respondent No. 4 with effect from 15-8-2006. On the other hand, the writ-petitioner joined a Development Project under the name and style "Horticulture Development Project" in 1997 and subsequently the writ-petitioner's post was temporarily transferred to the Revenue budget and he was temporarily appointed in the post of Revenue setup albeit his post was not included in the “বাংলাদেশ কৃষি গবেষণা ইনষ্টিটিউট (কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ১৯৯০” and in the BARI Organogram and the post of the writ-petitioner was created and included in “বাংলাদেশ কৃষি গবেষণা ইনষ্টিটিউট (কর্মচারী-কর্মচারী) চাকুরী প্রবিধানমালা, ২০১১” and his post was made permanent by the order of the Ministry of Agriculture under Memo No. গবেষণা-১/চাকুরী/রাজস্বখাত-২৮/২০০০ dated 23-1-2012 with effect from 1-6-2012 and, therefore, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is just and proper in accordance with law. He further submitted that the writ-petitioner was appointed as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in Development Project, namely “উদ্যান উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প (বারী অংশ)” and the duration of the project expired on 31-12-1999 the Ministry of Agriculture by its Memo dated 04-11-2003, temporarily transferred 44 posts including the post of writ-petitioner to the Revenue budget and sanction on year-to-year retention basis with retrospective effect since 1-1-2000 under certain terms and conditions mentioned in the Memo dated 4-11-2003 issued by the Ministry of Agriculture and violating the relevant provisions directly appointed the writ-petitioner to the post of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) on temporary retention basis by its Memo dated 16-4-2005 and at that point of time there were 2 (two) posts of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in BARI Organogram and such BARI authority in his appointment letter imposed a condition to the effect that  “রাজস্বখাতে স্থানান্তরিত সহকারী পরিচালক (অর্থ ও হিসাব) পদটি স্থায়ী হওয়ার পর সন্তোষজনকভাবে কার্য সম্পাদন সাপেক্ষে তাহাকে চাকুরীতে স্থায়ী করা হইবে” and included in the Service Regulations of 2011 there was no scope to regularise his post prior 2011 and the BARI authority did not take any approval from the Selection Committee or the DPC for regularisation of his service as per “উন্নয়ন প্রকল্প হইতে রাজস্ব বাজেট স্থানান্তরিত পদের পদধারীদের নিয়মিতকরণ ও জেষ্ঠ্যতা নির্ধারণ বিধিমালা, ২০০৫”. So, the order of regularisation dated 24-5-2006 of the service of the writ-petitioner is illegal and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He further submitted that admittedly writ-respondent No. 4 was appointed and joined as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) on 15-8-2006 against the substantive vacant post and, as such, writ-respondent No. 4 is undoubtedly senior to the writ petitioner, but the BARI authority illegally deprived writ-respondent No.4 of his due promotion and promoted the writ-petitioner to the post of Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) by the order dated 9-9-2012 made by the Director-General of BARI which is ex-facie illegal and, as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He further submitted that although chapter-7 of the Service Regulation, 2011 is captioned “সাধারণ আচরণ ও শৃঙ্খলা” yet the fact remains that any order can be appealed before the higher authority as per Regulation-46 of the Service Regulation, 2011 and that preferring an appeal to the higher authority arising out of any promotion matter as in the present instance to the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture by writ-respondent No. 4 has not been debarred by Regulation-46, regard being had to the language of Clause (Ka), of Sub-Regulation (2), Regulation-46 of the Service Regulation, 2011. Clause (Ka) of Regulation-46(2) provides “এই প্রবিধানমালার নির্ধারিত পদ্ধতি পালন করা হইয়াছে কিনা না হইয়া থাকলে উহার কারণে ন্যায় বিচারের হানি হয়েছে কিনা”. This provision engrafted therein clearly indicates that the appellate authority shall consider whether the prescribed procedure has been followed under the Service Regulations, 2011 and in the case of failure to follow the prescribed procedure thereunder, whether there has been a failure of justice for that reason and this Clause-(Ka) leaves no room for doubt that the appeal to the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture preferred by writ-respondent No. 4 was very much competent as such the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He submitted that admittedly writ-respondent No. 4 did not prefer any review application to the Director-General of BARI as contemplated by Regulation-47 of the Service Regulation, 2011, and instead preferred an appeal under regulation 46 against the order of promotion of the writ-petitioner dated 9-9-2012 and the appeal was duly disposed of by the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture, on the basis of report- dated 29-5-2013 submitted by the three Members Inquiry Committee and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He submitted that the BARI authority formed a three Member Committee to deter-mine the inter-se seniority of writ-petitioner and writ-respondent No. 4 and that committee, after hearing the parties and perusing the relevant documents and papers submitted by them, made a report dated 5-9-2012 to the Director-General, BARI recommending fixation of inter-se seniority of the parties by the Ministry of Public Administration, but for some mysterious and cryptic reasons, the Director-General, BARI himself snubbed the report of the committee and promoted the writ petitioner to the post of Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) on 9-9-2012 by superseding writ-respondent No. 4 and this action indicates the mala fide intention on the part of the Director-General, BARI and, as such, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 11959 of 2013 is sustainable in law. He submitted that writ-respondent No. 4 being senior to the writ petitioner, got selection grade scale of Taka 15,000 — 26,200 on 13-12-2010 with effect from 15-8-2010, but the writ-petitioner did not get the selection grade scale; the appellate authority having considered the pros and cons of the matter and regard being had to the seniority of writ-respondent No. 4, rescinded the order of promotion of the writ petitioner dated 9-9-2012 and directed the writ-respondent No. 2 take necessary step for promotion of writ-respondent No. 4 within 30 working days and, as such, the High Court Division did not commit any error of law in discharging the Rule Nisi and, therefore, the judgment and order to the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He submitted that this was a writ of certiorari wherein the scope of interference of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution is very limited and in this regard in the case of the Government of Bangladesh vs Md Afsar Ali reported in 58 DLR (AD) 107, the Appellate Division has held that the High Court Division can interfere with the findings of fact arrived at by the inferior Tribunal only when it can be shown that the findings are based on no evidence or non-consideration of material evidence. As the impugned order does not come within the purview of the ratio enunciated in the aforesaid decision, the writ-petitioner has no legs to stand and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is tenable in law. He submitted that admittedly the writ-petitioner first joined as Assistant Director (Accounts) in Horticulture Development Project under BARI on 15-3-1997 and the duration of the project eventually ended on 31-12-1999 and 44 posts of the project including the post of the writ-petitioner were transferred from the Development Budget to the Revenue Budget with effect from 1-1-2000. After transfer, the post of the writ- petitioner to the revenue set-up was kept on year-to-year retention basis till 31st May, 2012, writ-respondent No.3 by office order contained in Memo dated 3-5-2006 regularised the writ- petitioner in the service of BARI as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in violation of the provisions of the Sub-Rule (3) of Rule-4 of the Rules of 2005. Sub-rule (3) of rule 4 of the Rules of 2005 contemplates that “কর্ম কমিশনের আওতাভুক্ত কোন পদে কমিশনের সুপারিশক্রমে এবং কমিশনের আওতা বহির্ভূত কোন পদে বিভাগীয় পদোন্নতি বা বাছাই কমিটির সুপারিশক্রমে নিয়মিত করিতে হইবে।” Undeniably the post is within the remits of the Public Service Commission and that being so for regularising the service of the writ-petitioner the recommendation of the DPC or the Selection Committee, as the case may be is a must, but admittedly no recommendation of the DPC or the Selection Committee, as the case may be was obtained prior to regularisation of the service of the writ- petitioner in BARI which was flagrant violation of rule 4(3) of the Rules of 2005 and as per rule-5(1) of the Rules of 2005, the Seniority of any regularised officer or employee shall be calculated from the date of his regularisation in the service and as the writ-petitioner was regularised in the service of BARI on 24-5-2006 illegally, the provision of rule 5(1) cannot be called in aid in this respect. The DPC in its meeting dated 9-9-2012 unanimously recommended the writ-petitioner for promotion to the post of the Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) which was also ratified by the Management Board of BARI in its 50th General Meeting on the very date 9-9-2012 and on the same date the Director-General, BARI promoted the writ-petitioner to the post of Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) and on that very date he joined his promotion post. In this event it is clear that the BARI was in an unusual hurry to promote the writ-petitioner to the next higher post without caring for the legality or otherwise of the regularisation of the service of the writ petitioner. In the organogram of BARI there were 2 (two) sanctioned posts of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) in BARI at the relevant time. Indisputably writ-respondent No. 4 and one Md Yunus Ali, Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) were holding those posts at that time and there was no substantive or permanent third post of Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) till its creation and inclusion in the service Regulations of 2011. The post of the writ-petitioner was kept on year-to-year retention basis till 31-5-2012 and against this backdrop, the question of regularisation of the writ-petitioner as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) of BARI on 24-5-2006 was out of the question. Accordingly, after framing of the Service Regulation, 2011 the post of the writ-petitioner was made substantive and permanent on 1-6-2012. In this regard the Ministry of Public Administration by its Memo dated 17-5-2010 informed the Ministry of Agriculture that “নিয়োগ বিধি চূড়ান্ত না হওয়া দরুন্ত পদগুলি স্থায়ী করণের কোন অবকাশ নেই।”and, as such, the BARI could not promote the writ-petitioner to the post of the Senior Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) unless he had completed a minimum of 5 (five) years' service as Assistant Director (Finance and Accounts) and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law. He lastly submitted that according to Regulation 46(1) the appellate authority can hear any appeal preferred against any order by an aggrieved employee or officer and the appeal need not be confined to a matter arising out of disciplinary proceedings only and in the present case admittedly the Director-General, BARI is subordinate to the Secretary of the Ministry of Agriculture who is the controlling and appointing authority of the Director-General BARI and he is the appellate authority of the Director-General of BARI and Clause (Ka) of Regulation 46(2) provides that the appellate authority will consider accordingly and writ-respondent No. 4 rightly preferred appeal to the appellate authority the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture and the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture who was legally justified in forming a 3 (three) member inquiry committee to inquire into the matter of the appeal and the committee properly inquired the matter and heard the writ-petitioner, writ respondent No. 4 and also the Director-General, BARI and after hearing made a report, and on the basis of the inquiry report the Secretary, Ministry of Agriculture as appellate authority passed the impugned order which is just and proper and, as such, the judgment and order of the High Court Division is sustainable in law.
